claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA is single-phase BCC.
The baseline alloy has high density and insufficient room-temperature ductility, with brittle fracture behavior.
Adding 1.0–2.0 at.% Si will precipitate a continuous reticulated network of (Hf,Ti,Zr)5Si3-type intermetallics.
The Si-induced intermetallic network will be concentrated at grain boundaries and triple junctions.
Adding 1.5 at.% Si by arc melting and homogenization annealing is the proposed intervention.
Annealing at 1200°C for 24 hours followed by water quenching will stabilize the intermetallic network.
The structural mediator is a percolating reticulated network of (Hf,Ti,Zr)5Si3 Laves-like or silicide phases.
The brittle silicide network will deflect propagating cracks.
Ductile BCC matrix ligaments will bridge cracks around the silicide network.
Crack deflection and bridging will increase fracture-surface area and energy dissipation.
Solid-solution hardening would uniformly increase yield strength but typically further reduce ductility.
Si addition will increase room-temperature compressive yield strength by 15–25% relative to the baseline.
Si addition will significantly increase compressive plastic strain to failure relative to the baseline.
Si addition will increase bulk density by less than 1%.
The small density penalty is attributed to Si having low atomic mass relative to Hf and Zr.
The baseline alloy has less than 2% room-temperature plastic strain and fails by brittle cleavage.
The network mechanism requires Si content above an approximately 0.5 at.% nucleation threshold and below an approximately 2.5 at.% upper limit.
The proposed mechanism fails if Si remains fully dissolved or forms only isolated particles.
Adding 1.5 at.% Zr provides a control that experiences only solid-solution hardening and does not form silicides.

A statistically indistinguishable mechanical response between the Si-doped and Zr-doped samples, or cleavage through an observed silicide network rather than crack deflection or bridging, would falsify the proposed phase-structure mechanism.

contradictions.description: The precipitate is identified as an (Hf,Ti,Zr)5Si3-type silicide but is also called 'Laves-like.' A 5:3 silicide and a conventional Laves phase are distinct phase descriptions, leaving the proposed mediator internally ambiguous.
